claim: The GC design moved from an epoch-based reclamation (EBR) core that encoded generation in the object key (`blobs/<H>/<g>`) and required a `404→LIST` degraded read path, durable per-hash floors, and Keeper-fenced `safe_epoch`, to an incarnation model that moves the resurrection marker into the object body and deletion precision into the backend token, eliminating generation from any key and removing the `404→LIST` path entirely.

The GC in-degree model replaced a bare integer refcount with a source-edge multiset (`+`/`-` deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)`); the fold computes net in-degree from the edge multiset, and the `BlobInDegreeMatchesActiveManifests` TLA+ invariant asserts the multiset exactly equals the active manifests referencing the blob, turning the `+`-not-yet-durable race into a pending-fold problem rather than a guard problem.

Three fixes for the GC-registry monotone-growth problem were rejected before the shard-incarnation redesign: (1) writer deregisters at `dropNamespace` — unsafe because the removal `-1` in-degree edges would be lost if the namespace vanished from discovery before GC folded that window; (2) GC hard-deregisters when 'empty + settled' — indistinguishable from a live table between CREATE and its first INSERT; (3) shard-object deletion on the path-keyed cursor — an ABA hazard where a recreated shard resets `shard_version` to 0 and an old sealed cursor silently skips the new incarnation's events.

`CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla` checks `INV_NO_DANGLING` and `INV_NO_ORPHAN_EDGE` across 724,944 distinct states and proves that two orthogonal coordinates (a durable never-reused `incarnation` stamped at shard creation, and the pool-global GC `round`) are both necessary; three negative controls (`SabotageNewbornNoFloor`, `SabotagePathKeyedCursor`, `SabotageDeleteBeforeFold`) each show a counterexample when one coordinate is removed.

The B140 dangle was caused by `reuseBlob` (the adopt operation) transferring the blob hash but not the `cas_owner` protection, so an adopted blob's protection stayed bound to the retired byte-writer and GC reclaimed it under a still-in-flight adopter; `system.content_addressed_log` (B170) pinned the precise dangle event with its token and timing.

An aggressive test GC cadence exceeded the fixed iteration cap of 8 in `resolveAndResurrectGeneration`, producing `CORRUPTED_DATA` failures in ordinary insert/mutation tests; the soak surfaced 33 failures from this single root cause and the fix was a one-line cap change from 8 to 256.

A 2026-06-20 soak reported 1.6M `S3WriteRequestsErrors` and 94 `fsck dangling` after a chaos window; forensic analysis showed all 922,772 GC deletes had `indeg_at_recheck=0`, the errors were ~1.57M by-design `PreconditionFailed` (412) CAS contention on root-shard manifests, and the 94 dangling was a transient read-unavailability false-positive (429/503 load shedding) whose 180s settle budget was too short under write load.

The attempt-scoped-generation fix moved all decision-bearing round artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/…` rather than the narrower original proposal of attempt-scoping only the four `gc/gen/<gen>/…` write-once artifacts, because `retired` is a writer-facing publish-gate input that `RetireView::refresh` LISTs and writers consult on the commit path, so a stale retired set from a deposed leader under its own `(round, fence_seq)` could otherwise influence live writers.

Five same-class defect hardening findings (H1-H5) followed the B85/B87 fixes: H1 four unchecked `resolvePartGenKeyForRead` call sites in `getLastModified` could wedge `clearOldTemporaryDirectories` on DROP; H2/H3 two sites threw `LOGICAL_ERROR` for benign concurrent DROP/DETACH races that should have thrown recoverable `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`; H4 `replaceFile` lacked the `is_part_dir` directory delegation `moveFile` had just received; H5 `ContentAddressedGC::listLivePartIds` did a LIST-then-read without swallowing a concurrently-dropped ref.

A 2026-06-19 baseline determination against the pre-refactor binary found 68 unique failures in the `transactions` and `text-index` test families identically reproduced on the unrefactored binary, confirming they were pre-existing CA gaps (B182, B183) rather than regressions, so the refactor was declared regression-clean without any code change.

A 2026-06-22 model currency audit found no old-design cruft in any live TLA+ model, but found three models stale against shipped code around the B171 precommit-reachability mechanism — `CaBuildWatermark.tla`, `CaBuildWatermarkNum.tla`, `CaResurrectLiveness.tla` — and documented dispositions (mark stale; repurpose the watermark floor lemma for precommit-ref reclaim liveness) rather than deleting the models, preserving proof history.

CAS's condemned detection is a per-hash `.meta` point-read (`BlobMeta{version, state, condemn_round, size}` with `MetaState::Clean`/`Condemned`), not a writer-side retired-view cache; the earlier `Store::syncRetiredView`/`observed_gc_round`/`view_gate` machinery and the `MountLease.observed_gc_round` field are removed entirely. GC always writes a `Condemned` meta before ever deleting the body, so an absent meta reads exactly as live as a `Clean` one.

The writer consults the per-hash `.meta` with a single GET (`loadMeta`) only at `Build::observeAndAdmit` (dedup-hit/adopt path) and `Build::uploadFromSource` (fresh-upload/condemned-displacement path); a `Clean` or absent meta is adopted for free, a `Condemned` meta throws `ABORTED` so the caller re-uploads from source (INV-1) rather than reading the dying object.

EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE manifest-trust adoption: for a tokenless W-EVIDENCE dependency naming a blob referenced by a live committed source manifest, `Build::promote` trusts the durable manifest edge (`isTrustedAdopt`) with NO per-file HEAD/GET, because the source pins the blob (in-degree >= 1, GC cannot condemn it) and this build's own precommit edge is re-proved live at the promote owner-liveness gate before the trust fires; `copyForwardFromCondemned`/`isCopyForwardableTokenless` are deleted as a result.

The manifest-trust adoption trade-off (D4 relink trust model, ordinary ReplicatedMergeTree interserver trust) means a genuinely-absent adopted blob is no longer caught at promote time — it becomes an fsck `dangling` finding instead of a promote `ABORTED`; this is verified unreachable in production by source-pin plus durable-edge, backed by an independent EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE consult and a per-test reachability proof. This also incidentally fixed the S13 soak-run-3 liveness brick where `republishRef -> promote ABORTED (condemned)` had left a table readonly forever.

The flat-combining shard-mutation queue (`Store::mutateShard`) serializes intra-server writers per `(namespace, shard)`: the caller finding the queue leaderless flushes batches (one read, apply-all in order with per-closure snapshot isolation, one `casPut`) until its own item completes; the carve runs after the flush's first read so S3 read latency IS the batching window, turning the old positive-feedback conflict loop under load into a negative one. At most one mutation per ref name is allowed per flush; `WholeShard` closures (trim, fence, dropNamespace, reclaim) and create-if-absent flushes run solo.

Promote's publish-gate obligations (MR-1/MR-2/MR-3) apply only to the non-tokened evidence/copy-forward dependency subset since EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE: MR-1 consults durable deleted-token history, not only a cached retired set; MR-2/F1 re-validates the dependency's current physical state (still present, still carrying the originally-observed token, not merely 'not condemned when first seen'); MR-3/F2 requires bottom-up tree publish so a manifest may publish only when every direct child is present and non-condemned at publish time. A tokened dependency gets zero promote-time re-validation against any of these.

`INV-2` (precommit-first / reachability-before-content): the build-root precommit must be published before any pool content GET/HEAD/PUT of the build's content; the full write ordering stages blobs into local temp files, then makes the edge-bearing manifest body durable via `stageManifest`, then lands the owner event via `precommitAdd`, and only then do blob uploads reach the pool. A writer dying mid-upload therefore leaves blobs whose edges already exist in a folded body, so there is no structural 'orphan blob' class — an object in `blobs/` with no edge-bearing body in history should be impossible and fsck may treat one as an anomaly.

Since Task 5's `supportsAtomicFileWrites` capability, `VersionMetadataOnDisk::storeInfoToDataPartStorage` writes `txn_version.txt` as a single atomic `writeFile` with no `.tmp` file and no `replaceFile` call; `ContentAddressedTransaction::moveFile`'s legacy mutable-per-part-file destination routing is dead code in production for CA, still present pending a later mechanical sweep but unreached by any current write path.

Since the all-tree part-files migration, filling in the creation CSN on COMMIT and locking/unlocking the removal TID on an already-committed part are ordinary committed-ref standalone writes through `repointRef`, not a special mutable-only case: every OTHER committed manifest entry is carried forward and a byte-identical rewrite resolves through `repointRef`'s byte-equal check with zero pool mutations.

An uncommitted INSERT inside an open transaction still publishes a CAS ref whose blobs stay GC-reachable via a `WriteSession` pin until the ref lands; the part is logically invisible via its `txn_version.txt` creation CSN. ROLLBACK removes the ref, after which the blobs become GC-eligible.

A transactional merge/mutation spanning multiple parts is keyed by a per-part staging map, `parts: (namespace, ref) -> PartStaging`, rather than a single `(table_uuid, part_name)`; a deferred rename (`tmp_merge_X -> X`) moves the staging entry to the destination key and merges it with any destination entry a deferred-window `txn_version.txt` write already created. `commit` takes the `gc_lock` once and iterates `parts`, applying the whole-part publish or the mutable-only branch per entry.

A transactional multi-part commit is not filesystem-atomic on CAS: MVCC visibility is gated by the per-part CSN/TID in `txn_version.txt`, not by disk-op atomicity, so CAS may publish parts one at a time; a crash mid-commit leaves some refs published and some not, and orphan refs are GC-reclaimed exactly as any uncommitted-then-abandoned build (B122).

`stageManifest`'s inline caps, enforced fail-closed before any body write (OQ7): max entries per manifest 1,048,576; max encoded manifest size 256 MiB; max total inline bytes per manifest 16 MiB; max single inline entry 1 MiB.

Manifest backpressure (B164b): when a root shard's encoded size crosses `manifest_soft_limit`, `mutateShard` introduces a linear write delay for writer-origin mutations (0 at the soft limit, `manifest_max_delay_ms` near `manifest_hard_limit`); at or above `manifest_hard_limit` the mutation is rejected `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; GC mutations are never delayed; a batch at the hard limit degrades to solo re-flushes so only the offending mutation is rejected and co-batched neighbors proceed.

Rejected writer-protocol designs: `cas_owner` S3-metadata + `protectedByLiveBuild` guard (adopt did not transfer ownership, protection was revocable); a per-build heartbeat object at `builds/<build_id>` (leaked on successful publish, broke `DeletedCandidateDoesNotReappear`); `Build::resurrect` via GET-from-existing (raced GC delete in the HEAD-to-GET window); retaining full blob bodies in RAM (rejected on memory grounds for gigabyte column blobs); server-side copy/`UploadPartCopy` for bodyless re-stamp (dropped once the per-server watermark made bodyless re-stamp unnecessary; MinIO has known `UploadPartCopy` gaps); publish-at-precommit double-write (would add a second manifest PUT per part).

Open TODOs in the writer protocol: B172 (S3 staging area + server-side copy to remove the local scratch-dir requirement), the B199-S2 TLA+ gate extending `CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla` for the inline-closure fold barrier, plain non-replicated mutation publish still running under the `data_parts` lock (B151's fix covers only replicated paths), and a `farewell` on graceful shutdown to retire the epoch immediately instead of waiting for K=2 frozen-`seq` GC detection.

GC's raw baseline rebuild condemns nothing: it only rebuilds cursors and edges. An earlier version ended the pass by LISTing `blobs/` and condemning every physically-present body outside the rebuilt edge set, but this was found unsafe (r5-finding-4) because both legs of the traversal (owner replay and the trimmed-but-live manifest pass) are listing-driven, so a store that omits a durable key from one enumeration hides a live owner while the same pass condemns the blob that owner pins — an observed real failure mode (the `0x1430c` shape), not a hypothetical.

GC baseline rebuild is deliberately over-protective rather than under-protective: a build alive across journal trim has no journal evidence, so its manifests look unowned; the rebuild includes edges for every unowned manifest that is not provably build-dead, over-protecting rather than risking under-count. An unowned manifest that later dies with no journal evidence leaks its blob's edges for one bounded rebuild-to-rebuild window, `fsck`-visible as `unaccounted` — preferred to violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY`.
Before generation retention (B174) was added, a 12h soak measured `gc/` bookkeeping at 82% of pool storage (2822 retained generations, roughly 3.7 MiB/shard/generation), dwarfing actual data 8:1.

Patch parts / lightweight deletes are first-class GC reachability roots: a patch manifest references the base part's patched data columns plus its own delta blobs, and while a patch ref is active it transitively keeps alive both its own delta blobs and the base blobs it references, even if the base part is otherwise superseded, provided the MARK walk treats patch manifests as roots. When a patch is materialized into the base via merge, the patch ref is released and its uniquely-owned delta blobs become sweepable. Patch-on-content-addressed-base is flagged as not yet fully model-checked in the v3 design's residual-risk list.

A stateless/ref-less reader that attaches by reading the catalog and registers no `/parts` ref is invisible to the per-process `use_count()==1` MARK-union fence, which is a valid cross-node fence only for replicas holding a `/parts` ref; owning replicas can release refs after `old_parts_lifetime` (480s) mid-SELECT, sweeping the manifest/blobs out from under the read. The preferred fix is an ephemeral reader pin (a Keeper node or equivalent) created at query start naming the parts/snapshot read, auto-released on session end/crash; this is distinct from the lost-replica timeout, which is a genuine leak needing a separate long-dead-replica reaping rule.

docs/superpowers/cas/05-formats-and-backend.md's own DONE/TODO/REJECTED summary table records GCS generation-token binding as DONE 2026-07-03 (via `http_client = gcs_hmac`, a GOOG4-HMAC signer plus a wire-boundary conditional dialect that maps the response ETag to the generation, live-validated end to end), which contradicts the earlier prose in the same document describing GCS binding as deferred and fail-closed pending `Cas::Probe` validation — a live doc-internal drift the consolidation should resolve in favor of the DONE status.

`CaIncarnationProofCore.tla` used Apalache 0.58.0 to verify an inductive invariant `IndInv` (19 conjuncts) for a pre-B91, token-only fragment of the GC core: base case (`Init => IndInv`) and step check (`IndInv => IndInv'`) both held, which is stronger than TLC bounded checking because the step check quantifies over all states satisfying `IndInv` at fixed bounds regardless of trace depth; the model was removed 2026-07-22 as stale and unverifiable in an environment without an Apalache binary.

The heart conjunct of the Apalache inductive invariant, `InflightCurrentUnreferenced` (a delete message in flight for a still-current token implies no folded root edge and no unfolded add past the cursor), was proven irredundant by a negative control; dropping the `W-REVALIDATE` re-observation conjunct from `WPublish` produces a counterexample breaking `NoDangle`, machine-checking the F1 re-observation requirement.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` modeled a bug (H1b) where an in-degree completion-seal cursor persisted at `foldCursor` instead of `max(foldCursor, fenceVersion)` caused a re-fold of an already-absorbed fence-window removal, driving the integer in-degree counter to -1 (`INV_INDEG_NONNEGATIVE` violated, mapping to `CORRUPTED_DATA` in C++); the design decision was that the `Seal` action must advance the persisted cursor to `fenceVersion`, not remain at `foldCursor`.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` was removed 2026-07-22 because the shipped in-degree design no longer accumulates a non-idempotent integer delta stream: `CasBlobInDegree.cpp` computes in-degree via an idempotent two-cursor presence-set merge keyed by `(blob_hash, source_id)` where the surviving-edge count is an unsigned integer that structurally cannot go negative, so the underflow hazard the model existed to catch is now structurally impossible.

Three B167 build-watermark models (`CaResurrectLiveness.tla`, `CaBuildWatermark.tla`, `CaBuildWatermarkNum.tla`), all removed 2026-07-21, proved that resurrect liveness requires a guard blocking GC from re-condemning a freshly-owned incarnation during the non-atomic upload-to-publish span (the B167 livelock: dedup hit on a stale incarnation is deleted, the fresh re-upload is re-condemned by GC without a guard, looping forever); their safety role fully migrated into `CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla`'s precommit-first reachability mechanism, which replaced the modeled per-candidate blob-guard and condemn-time `HeartbeatGuard` that were never fully implemented.

The B167 watermark models established that `build_seq` must be allocated from a monotone counter, not merely a unique one: a non-monotone allocation lets the active-set floor (`min_active`) be pulled back below a finished build's sequence, re-protecting an already-condemned blob (a leak); this monotone-`build_seq` floor lemma survives in shipped code for precommit-ref reclaim (`Gc::prefixEligible` / the `BuildPrefix` watermark floor in `CasGc.cpp`), even though the blob-protection use case it was built for was replaced.

When asserting that a TLA+ sabotage config produces the expected counterexample, the runner scripts must grep the TLC log for a NAMED violation (`Invariant/Property/Action property <X> is violated`) and never trust a bare nonzero exit code, because TLC also exits nonzero on a parse error, an unspecified successor state, or a deadlock report — exactly how a broken model can masquerade as a working sabotage; this exact failure mode hid a live parse bug in `CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla` on 2026-07-28.

TLA+ models run from `docs/superpowers/models/` with the TLC jar expected at `../../../tmp/tla2tools.jar` (v2.19) and the Apalache binary at `../../../tmp/apalache/bin/apalache-mc` (v0.58.0+); runners are either suite runners that take no arguments and assert every expected outcome by invariant/property name (`run_refsnaplog.sh`, `run_mount.sh`, `run_buildrootprecommit.sh`, etc.) or single-config drivers that take a cfg as `$1` and assert nothing themselves (`run_tlc.sh`, `run_gc_partmanifest.sh`, `run_ackfloor.sh`).

`CaGcAckFloorCore.tla`'s `SabotageClampNoSuppress` config, which removes the `~clampedL` graduation guard, reproduces the 2026-07-03 night incident of 31 dangling blobs as an `INV_NO_DANGLE` counterexample; the shipped clamp-suppression guard (`suppress_destructive` gating `Gc::graduationDue`, `CasGc.cpp:1360`) blocks graduation and pending deletes while any shard is clamped, so held refs persist in `landed` until a later clamp-free pass consumes them.

A 2026-07-19 post-fix live chaos-soak measurement (workers=6, per-operation-unit attribution via ProfileEvents/part_log/content_addressed_garbage_collection_log) found a GC success round costs ~55-100x more per unit than a single INSERT/MERGE/MUTATE — not from PUTs (GC issues almost none) but from GET+HEAD volume in the retire/recheck verification pipeline ($0.00725/round vs $0.000085/INSERT); DownloadPart (replication fetch) was the cheapest unit at ~24x cheaper than an INSERT, confirming it as a lightweight metadata-level operation.

In the same 2026-07-19 measurement window, aggregate request cost (request pricing only) was approximately $15.13, with CAS-internal housekeeping (per-blob `.meta` sidecar PUTs, cas/manifests, cas/refs, gc/gen attempt/outcome records) as the single largest line item at $5.64 (1,128,865 PUTs) -- larger than the INSERT bucket itself, and not previously broken out as its own cost driver.

Attributing S3 PUTs to MergeParts/MutatePart requires a query_id-decoding technique because part_log's own ProfileEvents never captures a nonzero PUT for those event types: the upload count is recovered by matching blob_storage_log's synthetic `<table_uuid>::<part_name>` query_id against part_log by part name (documented in the analyzing-cas-health skill and utils/ca-soak/scenarios/BACKLOG.md's 2026-07-19 'S3 PUT budget' entry).

The P9 GC 404-HEAD-storm fix's original mechanism, GcSnap::forget node-pruning, was later removed and superseded by the source-edge-set GC model (which has no persisted node registry to forget from); the ~90%-of-read-ops savings it was credited with is a historical measurement basis, not tied to a currently-existing mechanism.

A 4h active-workload chaos soak at WORKERS=6 fills the disk in ~60-90 min; root cause is rustfs#3231 (upstream, open): overwriting a >128 KiB object in an un-versioned bucket leaks the previous incarnation's data directory, so every `casPut` of a `cas/refs/<...>/<shard>` body leaks one uuid dir (observed 1600+ dirs on one busy shard key; `cas/refs` reached 39 GB of a 45 GB pool vs 7.2 GB of real blob data), and the metacache walk over those dirs produces `list_merged err Io(timeout)` / `walk_dir timeout` LIST storms at ~600k files. Mitigation: WORKERS=2; durable fix is lowering ref-shard `casPut` rate (journal batching) and/or moving shard bodies under the 128 KiB inline threshold, or the upstream RustFS fix.

`ca-fsck` times out (>180s) at approximately a 150 GB pool because `ObjectStorageBackend::list` re-enumerates the whole `roots/` prefix per page, an O(N^2) cost in the manifest backlog; the fix is to paginate at the source and separate shard objects into a dedicated prefix.

`system.part_log`'s `NewPart` row shares the same underlying ProfileEvents as the originating `INSERT` query's `system.query_log` row (confirmed via `sumMap(ProfileEvents)` cross-checks), so summing them together double-counts S3/Cas cost; `MergeParts`/`MutatePart`/`DownloadPart` are genuinely additive on top of `query_log` because their originating `Optimize`/`Alter` query_log rows show zero S3 ProfileEvents (background execution is captured only by part_log).

`system.trace_log`'s three trace_types answer different questions and must not be conflated: `CPU` shows where processor cycles are spent (group by full stack, not just leaf frame); `Real` shows wall-clock time including blocking waits, where most top entries are healthy idle capacity and the useful signal is a thread blocked inside the product's own internal queue/lock; `Memory` samples allocation events (not resident memory), and its leaf frame is always the profiler's own capture routine, so the first one or two frames must be skipped before reading the real allocation site.

Cross-referencing generic S3-level counters (`S3PutObject`/`S3GetObject`/`S3HeadObject`/`S3ListObjects`/`DiskS3DeleteObjects`) against CAS's own semantic per-object-kind counters (`Cas{Blob,Gc,Manifest,Meta,Root,Other}{Put,Get,Head,Delete,List}`) in one soak session found the Cas-level counters covered PUT/GET/LIST far better than the query_log/part_log/GC-log attribution axis (77-96% vs 4-58%) because they are incremented at the S3-call site independent of ThreadGroup attribution, while HEAD stayed persistently under-attributed on both axes (~56%), left as an open question.

Every positive CAS scenario in the S01-S35 suite must satisfy: SQL correctness (all replicas match the scenario oracle's aggregates), storage correctness (`ca-fsck --detail` reports `dangling = 0`), GC safety (`ca-gc-dryrun` delete candidates are a subset of the `ca-fsck` unreachable set at quiescence), a clean event audit (`system.content_addressed_log` has no error-class event types), no `Failed` GC-round finish rows, no unbounded leftovers after forced GC, and no excessive resource growth beyond the scenario budget.

The soak harness's quiescence protocol before any checkpoint assertion is: pause all workers; `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` on both nodes and wait for `system.replication_queue` to be empty; wait for every `system.mutations` row to be `is_done` with no active `system.merges`; run `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` plus `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE TTL`; then drive CA GC to fixpoint by polling until the pool object set and `ca-fsck`'s `unreachable` field stop changing across successive rounds.

The soak harness's chaos model applies seeded faults defined by `{t_offset, target in {ch1,ch2,both,rustfs}, action in {kill-9, restart, pause/unpause}, duration}`; faults are bounded so a quiescent checkpoint is always reachable between them, and a server that does not recover within the bound is treated as a correctness failure, not a flake.

Both the shard decode cache and the `(ManifestId, Token)` manifest decode cache are memory-bounded by a wholesale clear rather than LRU eviction: once either cache grows past `SHARD_DECODE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` or `MANIFEST_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, the whole cache is cleared; entries re-populate on demand and a cleared entry is never incorrect, only slower (one extra HEAD plus GET).

The B115 `ReadBufferFromFileView` position-corruption bug was latent (not yet triggered) in `PackedFilesReader`, the only other in-tree consumer of `ReadBufferFromFileView`, because its current caller (`loadStatisticsPacked`) uses a sequential, non-seekable `CompressedReadBuffer` that never calls `setReadUntilPosition`; the fix is in place there too and the report flags this as upstream-relevant.

The CAS backup threat model defines five threats: T1 bucket/region loss, T2 operator error (`DROP TABLE`, bad mutation, wrong `rm`), T3 a CAS-layer bug (notably a GC bug deleting live data), T4 credential compromise, and T5 format dependence (whether restore requires a CAS-capable ClickHouse, any ClickHouse, or no ClickHouse at all).

For non-atomic bucket-sync backups, `gc/server-roots/<id>/epoch` (a `WriterEpochMonotoneUnique` durable-monotone counter) can be captured before manifests minted under a later epoch, letting a restored writer re-issue a used `writer_epoch`; the chosen backup design avoids this by never replicating identity objects at all, rather than sequencing the copy to take identity objects last.

No single backup tier covers the full threat matrix; the recommended composition is B1+B2 (in-pool `FREEZE`/retention-delayed-GC tier, near-free, a consistency anchor) plus the CAS-native backup pool (primary DR tier) plus native `BACKUP` at a rare weekly cadence (the only tier restorable without a CAS-capable binary), with logical export (Iceberg/Parquet) optionally as a fourth archival tier.

As an RTO optimization when a full fetch is too slow, the storage policy can combine a fresh writable CA disk with the backup pool mounted as a readonly disk (claiming no lease or epoch, under the fsck/ca-gc-dryrun discipline): reads work within minutes straight off the backup, writes go to the fresh pool from minute one, and fetch degrades into a background hot-partitions-first drain by ordinary move machinery.

In-place fail-over (mounting the backup bucket directly as the new production pool) is documented as a last resort that consumes the backup at the first `PUT`; if ever used, `fsck` must run before the first write, GC and thinning must stay disabled until an operator explicitly enables them, and a new backup chain to a third bucket must start immediately.

Comparing hot-tier consolidation snapshots via bare `checksums.txt` equality was rejected because MergeTree checksums are `CityHash128`, a non-cryptographic hash that must not gate a decision to skip reading bytes; inode witnesses / borg-style filesystem-identity caches were also rejected as side state alien to the CA model, whose identity primitive is re-hashing.

The optional age-based trickle warmer pushes blobs of hot parts older than a threshold `A` into the pool ahead of any snapshot, on the reasoning that a part surviving the young-merge window will likely reach the cold tier eventually; with the warmer on, consolidation degrades into publishing metadata only, and TTL moves become nearly free.

The classic `clickhouse-backup` (Altinity) freeze-and-copy mode is incompatible with CAS because there are no local metadata files and no filesystem shadow (shadow lives in-pool as refs); only its embedded mode, which wraps native `BACKUP`, applies.

A DR replica option is a `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica in another region with its own pool; fetch-by-relink applies only within one pool (`pool_uuid` equality), so a foreign-pool replica performs honest byte fetches, giving RPO ~ replication lag and RTO ~0, and covering T1/T4 but not T2 (it replicates `DROP TABLE` too).

Logical export (Iceberg/Parquet/datalake) is the ultimate independence tier (readable without ClickHouse, directly queryable by other engines) but is lossy: `AggregateFunction` states do not survive Parquet, and `LowCardinality`, codecs, skip indexes, projections, and physical `ORDER BY` layout are all lost; restore is a full re-insert, the longest RTO in the survey.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` isolated an in-degree-underflow hazard the large safety model could not express: the C++ accumulated blob in-degree as a non-idempotent integer delta stream, which could reach -1 (throwing `CORRUPTED_DATA`) when a completion-seal cursor persisted at the wrong position; the fix adopted an idempotent two-cursor presence-set merge, making the underflow structurally impossible, and the model was then removed because it described a design the code had abandoned.

GC registered defect R2: `PartWriteTxn`'s destructor unconditionally retired its build sequence, advancing the GC floor while the precommit grant's outcome was still uncertain, making an uncertain owner grant look dead; the fix is a duty queue with the failure direction inverted (settle then retire then pop), where any throw retains the duty and a full queue pins the floor, since an advanced floor is an irreversible authorization while a pinned one only costs latency.
GC observability gained per-phase timing during Stage B, which immediately found the fold seal being read five times per round where the design intended two.

An MSan log refuted the mount-fence observability spec's original premise: the real failure mode was Mode 2, a hung lease-renewal call that produces a silently expired fence and a silent re-arm, with no throw and no log on any transition; the spec went to rev.2 to address this, and was specced but not yet implemented as of the writing.
CI needed 6-hour-job-timeout sharding after a TSan lane finished 10,990/10,990 tests but was killed 16 seconds before it could report the result.

The design rule that generalizes the LIST-trust resolution: any input feeding an irreversible action must be structurally unable to authorize it wrongly, it may only delay it. A stale-but-honest observation is a true cut from the past whose induced errors fall toward retention/latency and are closed forward by ordering and a final re-check at the destructive site; a fabricated cut (omission under a permanent seal) corresponds to no point in time and can authorize destruction. LIST is only used in roles that satisfy this (work bound, witness set, genesis hint); the trusted verbs (exact-key reads, conditional writes) carry everything else.

A TLA+ model is deleted, not kept, once keeping it would assert a guarantee the shipped code no longer makes; false comfort (an unfaithful model implying a safety property the code does not actually provide) is treated as worse than having no proof at all.

CAS design work treats a proof of correctness as requiring an executable, reproducible counterexample: a test must be able to fail. A relink proved only by a flat blob count is worthless because a byte fetch onto a content-addressed disk also dedups and produces the same flat count, so that test cannot distinguish the mechanism under test from a working fallback.

CAS treats a plan as a hypothesis about how to proceed, not an authority: plans have been wrong in every round (a field placement that silently rebound positional initialisers, a prescribed proof that proved nothing, a step whose own authorization forbade it), so the person executing a plan is expected to notice when it is wrong and say so rather than execute it as written.

The CAS backend contract's `TOKEN ⟹ CONTENT` requirement (a repeated token implies unchanged bytes) is the one item that cannot be probed cheaply and is therefore a documented, unverified assumption on every backend, not enforced by the capability probe.

CAS refuses BACKUP via temporary hard links for Ordinary (non-UUID) databases with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, while Atomic databases back up normally; partition commands are refused outside an explicit allowlist (DROP_PARTITION, DROP_DETACHED_PARTITION, FORGET_PARTITION, ATTACH_PARTITION, REPLACE_PARTITION, MOVE_PARTITION, FETCH_PARTITION, FREEZE_*, UNFREEZE_*); `supportsChmod`/`supportsStat` are false and `getHardlinkCount` returns 0; bucket versioning must not be enabled and is probed and refused; and `<readonly>1</readonly>` disks take no mount claim, run no probe, no writes, and no GC.

`putDeterministicArtifact` is the write-once helper for GC objects whose bytes are a pure function of their inputs (source-edge runs, fold seals): a `putIfAbsent` precondition failure is resolved by reading the existing object back and comparing bytes — byte-equal means the writer's own replay landed and is adopted as a no-op, while divergent bytes throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` as an impossible case. It is deliberately not used for observation-bearing artifacts like GC outcome logs, which use first-durable-write-wins byte-adopt semantics instead, and never for blob bodies because the fresh-tag rule makes two attempts of the same logical create legitimately differ.

`claimOwnerOrThrow` binds `server_root_id` to `server_uuid` permanently via a decision table: an owner present with a `retired_at_ms` tombstone throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` refusing to resume; an owner present with a different uuid throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` naming the regenerated-uuid-file cause and remedies; an absent owner over a non-provably-empty subtree throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` for identity-lost-over-existing-data; and losing the `putIfAbsent` race re-reads, proceeding only if the winning uuid matches. "Provably empty" requires both an authoritative catalog naming no life owned by the srid and 1-key LIST probes finding nothing under `cas/manifests/<srid>/` or `roots/<srid>/`.
Part manifest caps are enforced before the body is written: 1,048,576 entries, 256 MiB of encoded text, 16 MiB total inline bytes, and 1 MiB per individual inline entry.

The ref-lane flush uses a per-table "wedge": at most one outstanding record per table holding the key and sealed bytes of a single conditional PUT whose outcome is unresolved. The next flush must resolve that exact key (via `resolveByExactGet`) before it may allocate a new transaction id, which is what realizes INV-14 (fail-closed on ambiguity) and prevents the ledger from ever silently creating a gap or double-publishing.

The part-write crash-point table enumerates nine distinct crash windows (C1-C9) and their cleanup owner: C1 staging leaves local temp files (cleaned unconditionally) or S3 staging objects (cleaned only by the mount's own next-mount staging sweep, never on abort); C2 post-stageManifest-pre-precommitAdd leaves an unreferenced manifest cleaned by best-effort delete or the orphan sweep backstop; C3 an Unresolved precommitAdd leaves a possibly-live binding whose body is never writer-deleted; C4 between precommitAdd and promote has no resume path (INV-10) and is removed by abandon or a fenced successor's stale-precommit sweep; C5 mid blob fan-out leaves already-uploaded blobs as GC-reclaimable debris with nothing merged; C6 an Unresolved promote append leaves `CommitState::Uncertain`, mapped by the relink layer to "retry the whole fetch"; C7 a later part throwing after earlier parts published triggers precise rollback of only the refs this call created; C8 a destroyed uncommitted transaction has its destructor abandon every open build (INV-19); C9 a namespace dropped mid-build sets one atomic flag so every further op fails closed at `requireAlive`. Every row leaks at worst; no row loses data or dangles.

In GC sharding, a shard with an empty delta bucket and no condemned entries in the parent summary copies the parent's run references verbatim ("pure carry", zero run I/O); a missing parent summary entry on a non-fresh pool is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never silently treated as zero.

Generation pruning (GC phase 13) keeps the last `gc_snap_generations_to_keep` generations (default 3; 0 keeps everything for forensics) and deletes wholesale by LIST-and-delete-everything under the generation prefix, bounded to 64 generations per round. A generation still referenced by the live seal is skipped but the cursor still advances past it regardless, so leak-freedom depends entirely on the post-CAS hand-off reclaim in phase 14.

The content-addressed disk configuration surface rejects unknown keys (with an explicit skip-list for generic object-storage-layer keys) and includes: `scratch_path` (default: server data path), `blob_hash` (default `cityhash128`, options `cityhash128`/`xxh3-128`/`sha256`, fixed at pool creation), `blob_hash_allow_new` (default `false`), `staging_backend` (default `local`; `s3` is opt-in and gated on the conditional-copy probe), `gc_meta_pool_size` (default 16), `manifest_sweep_list_budget_keys`/`manifest_sweep_delete_budget_keys` (default 1000/100), `dedup_cache_bytes` (default 64 MiB, 0 disables), `part_folder_cache_bytes`/`_max_entries`/`_max_entry_bytes` (default 64 MiB / 10000 / 16 MiB), `part_folder_validate` (default `always`; options `always`/`never`/`age <seconds>`), `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` (default 1 GiB), and `skip_access_check` (default `false`, skips the boot capability probe).

The walkthrough documents seven specific instances of documentation drift found and verified against the code while writing it: `03-writer-protocol.md:379-394` still describes a mutable `RefSidecar` file class (the mutable set is actually empty); `04-gc-protocol.md` still describes the round as fold->retire->fence->recheck->trim (it is actually 18 phases ending in one CAS) and still references the removed `Gc::reclaimDroppedShards`; `05-formats-and-backend.md` still describes binary `CABL`/`CATR` envelopes, protobuf, a mutable `cas_ref_shard` object and a `Tree` kind (the format is JSON text end-to-end with no `Tree` kind); `07-s3-budget.md:279-289` still shows one `cas/refs/` LIST per round and a retired-run write row (the implementation does two LISTs and has no separate retired object); `09-read-protocol.md` still references `Core/CasStore.cpp`, root shards, and a `mutable_files` sidecar (all three are gone); and `01-architecture.md:67-70,104-116` still describes blob identity as fixed `cityHash128` and manifests as protobuf (the hash algorithm is pluggable per blob and manifests are text).

Directory and existence operations under CAS avoid S3 LISTs almost entirely by answering from in-memory structures: `existsFile` on a part file is a manifest binary search on the cached view (0 cost); `existsDirectory` on a table dir uses `hasAnyRefWithPrefix` on the in-memory ref index (0); part-dir existence is a ref resolve (0); projection existence uses `hasDirectory` over sorted manifest entries (0); `listDirectory` on a table dir uses `listRefs` plus `listNamespaceFiles` (0 for refs); `listDirectory` on a part or projection is a prefix range over sorted manifest entries (0); `getFileSize`/`getLastModified` read the manifest entry or the ref's `published_at_ms` (0). Only `listDirectory` on the disk root, `store`, or `store/<u3>` falls through to a real mirrored S3 LIST (1 LIST) because those paths have no namespace anchor.

CAS discovery LISTs use fixed prefixes: `cas/ns/stream/`, `cas/ns/`, `cas/manifests/`, `blobs/` (deliberately without the algorithm segment so one recursive LIST covers every hash algorithm), `roots/`, and `gc/server-roots/`. The `staging/` prefix is a top-level sibling that no GC LIST ever touches — it is reclaimed only by its own server's next mount.

Namespace removal has no physical-empty handshake: the writer changes the catalog row from `Live` to `Removing`, appends the exact ref removals plus a `RemoveNamespace` op, and deletes nothing itself. GC's fold attaches cleanup evidence to that opaque life row, and only a later GC invocation's pre-fold drain exact-CAS-deletes the matching `Removing` catalog row before any successor plan can be published; the perpetual namespace janitor and orphan-manifest sweep reclaim the physical debris independently, and a same-name birth waits only for the catalog row to disappear.

`RefTableState` holds a copy-on-write map of committed rows, a set of precommits, an O(1) manifest-ownership index enforcing the one-owner-per-manifest invariant, a lifecycle (`Live`/`Removed`), the greatest applied transaction id, and O(1)-maintained body-size counters for admission. Two mutexes have a fixed lock order `ref_queue_mutex -> state_mutex`, never the reverse, and network I/O is never performed under `state_mutex`, so a reader sees either a whole transaction or none of it.

Ref-log snapshots publish in the background, best-effort, one in flight per table, once the tail exceeds `snapshot_log_count_threshold` (default 256 logs) or `snapshot_log_bytes_threshold` (default 1 MiB); publish failures arm per-table exponential backoff from 200 ms to 30 s.

Recovery of a ref table on first touch performs a paginated LIST of `cas/ns/stream/<life-id>/`, takes the greatest snapshot, replays every log strictly greater than it one transaction at a time, restarts on a vanished object (bounded at 3 attempts, treated as concurrent GC cleanup rather than corruption), and on an unclean boundary publishes a recovery seal snapshot at the synthetic id `{my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX}` before exposing the table, so that id dominates any straggler the dead epoch could still materialize.

The measured GET-cost formula for a folding GC round is exact: total `S3GetObject` = ref-log body GETs + manifest body GETs, i.e. `1 + edges_per_log`, which climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows; round trips equal `logs + edges` at a flat roughly 0.5 ms per round trip across a 140x request range, and a measured 416-round `Success` sample cost roughly $0.007 in total S3 charges.

A one-shot `CORRUPTED_DATA` error from a temp-fetch with an absent binding was observed once during the definitive consistency soak and flagged for investigation; it was not reproduced or root-caused during the round.

During the definitive consistency soak, a GC round (round 3) did zero work but still took 764 seconds, which was flagged as an observability gap (no signal distinguishing a genuinely idle round from a stalled one) rather than a correctness bug.

During a pure verbatim-relocation refactor (moving `CasMountRuntime`/`CasRefLedger` members between classes), the original member declaration order must be preserved exactly even when an agent proves an alternate order is equally safe: member order is observable construction/destruction behavior, and a relocation commit must not silently change it, so the original `ref_ledger`-before-`mount_runtime` order was restored via a follow-up commit rather than kept as the accidentally-reversed order.

dedupTrace independently traced the CAS write ordering in `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink`: the CAS commit (`renameParts`→`stageManifest`, line 976) strictly precedes the atomic Keeper dedup-token multi-op (line 985), so a failed CAS write leaves no dedup token behind; this refuted the initially-suspected "orphan-token" mechanism for the R3 data-loss regression, though the acked-then-lost data loss itself remained confirmed via a separate mechanism.

Scenario cards that check GC-reclaim progress mid-run (not just at the final checkpoint) must honor the condemn-grace period the same way the end-checkpoint does, or they miscount in-pipeline objects awaiting graduation as a leak; this miscalibration (not a product bug) caused a false-red S36 verdict and is a lesson for other scenario cards with mid-run reclaim assertions.

On GCS's S3-compatible XML surface signed with sigv4, none of the conditional operations CAS needs are enforced (create-if-absent, conditional overwrite, and conditional delete are all silently ignored — a wrong-ETag DELETE on GCS S3-compat actually deletes the object); the same HMAC credential pair, signed instead with GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 over the GCS XML endpoint, enforces all of them via `x-goog-if-generation-match`.

On GCS, `CompleteMultipartUpload` silently ignores `x-goog-if-generation-match` (both a `0`-against-existing and a wrong-generation precondition return 200 and overwrite), so conditional writes must not use multipart on GCS; `Compose` does enforce the precondition, so the production-grade large-blob path on GCS is: unconditional multipart-to-temporary-key, then a preconditioned `Compose(temp -> final)`, then delete the temp key.

The GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 signer was implemented as a sigv4 variant (renamed constants: `GOOG4` key prefix, `goog4_request` scope, `x-goog-date`/`x-goog-content-sha256` headers) plus a precondition-header mapping (`If-None-Match: *` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`; `If-Match: <etag>` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`) and token extraction from the `x-goog-generation` response header, letting the existing CAS S3 backend target GCS natively via a `http_client = gcs_hmac` opt-in and a `TokenType::Generation` token kind.

Three bugs were found and fixed while validating the GCS Generation binding end-to-end: (1) probe wrong-tokens were non-numeric, so the dialect's format guard killed the mount; (2) LIST-derived tokens on GCS are MD5 ETags (XML LIST bodies are not rewritten to generations), which would poison `If-Match` in GC, so list-derived tokens are disabled on generation-token stores; (3) the `Expect: 100-continue` handling did not recognize the GCS dialect header, creating a B118-class stall risk.

A `ca_ro` shadow disk declared in the server config breaks table load on restart with `UNKNOWN_DISK`; the workaround shipped for the GCS validation stand was a dedicated config (`fsck_only_gcs.xml`) that omits the shadow disk, with the real product fix tracked as a ROADMAP row.

As of the 2026-07-03 real-object-storage validation, gate #1 (multi-backend real-store validation) had AWS S3 and GCS both fully validated (probe + replication + two-phase reclaim + fsck clean); Azure had not been started, and GCS's production-grade follow-ups (compose finalize for >1 GiB conditional writes, `gcp_oauth` credential validation, generation-aware LIST discovery) were left as desirable, non-blocking rows.

A `LOGICAL_ERROR` "release before start" fires when Store teardown calls `stop()`/`doTerminate` on a mount-lease keeper whose `seq` is still 0 because `doStart` threw before completing; this is pure noise during an already-failing shutdown rather than a real defect signal, and the recommended fix is for `doTerminate` with `seq == 0` to be a quiet no-op.

During rev.7/rev.8 disk-lifecycle implementation, T7's implementer review found a real hole (I1): the observe/FSCK path could mint `_pool_meta` over a residual pool state, and the implementer's justification for why this was safe was factually wrong per the reviewer's independent re-verification; the fix flipped the polarity to fail-closed (mint-permission gate).

Mid-way through the rev.7 disk-lifecycle plan the user ordered a scope cut to a FORGET-only v1: the natural-erasure proof stack (~1500-2000 lines) was excised entirely (erasure is asserted, never machine-proven), documented as spec rev.8 with a 10-item excision list; TLA+ Model 1 (natural-erasure proof) was dropped while Model 2 (lifecycle/FORGET) remained the gating model, and the excision itself removed a net 1095 lines with a clean adversarial review.

The rev.8 disk-lifecycle whole-increment final review found two Important pre-release defects, both TOCTOU races around the `gc_scheduler_mutex`: (I-1) a manual `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN` admitted while the pool was `Live` could queue behind FORGET's `gc_scheduler_mutex` and, once granted, resume and run a full GC round against a since-decommissioned (`Vanished`) pool; (I-2) `runGcRebuildNow` did not take `gc_scheduler_mutex` at all, making a GC rebuild invisible to FORGET and able to durably write after FORGET believed all GC threads were stopped. Both were fixed with a lock-then-gate pattern (matching `gcStart`) plus RED-demo regression tests.

The rev.7/rev.8 disk-lifecycle work landed a `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` verb (with `GC STOP` / `GC START` companions) that unmounts a disk's pool by stopping all background CAS activity (GC, mount-lease renewal) and ejecting the disk, backed by a machine-checked (TLA+ Model 2) lifecycle state machine and an always-present `system.content_addressed_mounts`-style row per pool, rather than the previously-planned natural-erasure proof mechanism.

A pre-release v3 data-loss hole was found while modeling the deposed-leader path in TLA+: a deposed GC leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` call leaves stray-Clean freshness metadata over a `delete_pending` blob; a writer can then reuse the condemned blob's exact token, and the pending exact-token redelete for that token deletes the live reuse, violating `INV_NO_LOSS`. The fix made GC freshness metadata add-only (never `Condemned`->`Clean` on a spare leader; only a writer holding a fresh incarnation token may publish `Clean`), verified by a TLA+ witness plus 5 sabotage configurations including a `post_adoption_clear` case that produces an authentic 16-state 2-leader counterexample against the naive fix.

During the S3-native-staging end-to-end validation on RustFS, staged blobs were found to be stored without the 256-byte `CABL` envelope header — a data-corrupting bug invisible to 17 in-memory unit tests — fixed by dropping `logical_size`/`logical_hash` from the staging path and writing the header directly into the staging object ahead of hashing; a related fix introduced fresh-tag resurrect to close an `INV_NO_RETURN` self-condemn hole this staging change exposed.

The pluggable blob-hash Phase 1 design encodes the hash algorithm identifier directly in the blob's storage path (`blobs/<algo>/<shard>/<hex>`), records the pool's chosen algorithm in `PoolMeta`, and fail-close-validates that recorded algorithm against the disk's configured algorithm on every open, so an existing pool is never silently re-hashed under a different algorithm.

Attribution of the night's 11 concurrent GC clamps was: RustFS returned false 404s on HEAD during a metacache storm caused by the `rustfs#3231` overwrite-leak's directory bloat (00:37-00:55); the clamps rose with the storm and self-released when it subsided (~01:01), and the bodies the false 404s claimed were missing had never actually been deleted (no `tree_delete` for the pinned manifests). The full causal chain is: leak -> directory bloat -> metacache storm -> false 404s on HEAD -> GC clamps -> (pre-fix) graduation proceeding over unfolded landed events -> dangling blobs.

After weighing the clamp-attribution findings, the CAS `root_shards` default was raised from 8 back to 32 (the queue mechanism had already removed the contention argument for fewer shards; 32 shards yields a ~25 KB healthy journal tail with ~1.4x batching and 4x discovery-key fan-out), soak configs were raised to 64 shards for extra `rustfs#3231` margin, and `gc_trim_body_soft_limit` was restored from the 96 KiB experiment back to an 8 MiB backstop because the trim cap cannot bind body size at all — body size is cursor-age-bound (round-cadence-bound), not trim-bound, and the working trimmer is the 256-event count gate.

A `gc_fold_clamp` event (fields: namespace, shard, manifest, reason, at_version) was added per clamp occurrence to `content_addressed_log`, so that root-causing a GC clamp incident — previously an hour of event-log archaeology across archived server logs — becomes a single query.

E1 (relaxed replay of RefTableState) shipped as KEEP: the un-materialized overlay makes per-transaction scratch copies O(overlay) instead of O(N), reducing replay cost by 22-25% and strengthening the case for E3.

E2 (owned-manifest index for RefTableState) shipped as KEEP achieving flat O(1) BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit (~712-726 ns), at the honest cost of ScratchCopy +13 ns and BM_ReplayHistory regressing to 50,082 ns/row because the index overlay grows along the never-materializing replay tail; E3 was tasked to recover it.

E3 shipped as the simplified variant with no undo journal: `TrustedHistory` apply-mode does in-place mutation with poison-on-throw (replay-only, poison provably contained at all 3 callers), while `Full` keeps the verbatim two-phase copy; this cut BM_ReplayHistory from 50,082 to 1,725.58 ns/row (-96.6%, ~29x) with writer benches flat.

E4 (flat-vector base for RefTableState) was REVERTED after implementation: it only cleared Materialize's asymptotic cost 2x (O(NlogN)->O(N)) on a cost that is per-flush, never trace-visible, and N-budget-bounded, so simplicity won over the marginal gain.
E5 (mutate-in-place-when-uniquely-owned materialize) shipped as KEEP, cutting unique-owner materialize from O(N) to O(overlay) for both COW containers.
